    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open for today in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide, with the Sales Type column turned on.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  2. Expand {Sales-rep-B}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1}'s invoice shows one row under {Sales-rep-A}: Sales Type "Labor"; Labor Invoiced $200.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00, labor columns filled; Parts Invoiced and Parts Margin show a dash, not $0.00. {Sales-rep-A}'s summary row shows real sums (no dashes), $200.00 of labor, and counts the invoice once.
  • Step 2: {Work-order-1}'s invoice shows one row under {Sales-rep-B}: Sales Type "Parts"; Parts Invoiced $50.00; Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and Shop Supplies show a dash. {Sales-rep-B}'s summary row shows real sums (no dashes), $50.00 of parts, and counts the invoice once. The invoice is two rows, one under each representative.

The Sales By Representative spec, version 28 (12 Oct 2026, S9-N1), shows Labor Delta as 0.0 on a Parts row. Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 for the PRD (answer 24, quoted below): a dash on the Parts row. This case follows PRD version 11.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11266 (Story 2, Give a work order a separate Labor and Parts representative), story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R1: “When a work order is invoiced, the parts representative and the labor representative in effect are both captured on the invoice, by name.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”
  • S5-R4: “A Labor row is credited with Labor Invoiced, Labor Margin, labor-line fees and discounts, Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta and all of the invoice's Shop Supplies, including an amount typed by hand.”
  • S5-R5: “A Parts row is credited with Parts Invoiced, Parts Margin and part-line fees and discounts.”
  • S5-R11: “Two different people on one work order are always two rows.”
  • S5-R13: “A representative counts an invoice once, even when they have two rows for it. When two people split an invoice, each counts it once, so the representatives' invoice counts can add up to more than the shop's.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”
  • S5-R16: “A representative's summary row always shows real sums, never dashes.”
  • S2-R13: “"Sales Representative - Labor" is credited with the labor side of the invoice and "Sales Representative - Parts" with the parts side (Story 5).”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”

Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice total before tax is $980.00 (600.00 + 400.00 + 30.00 − 50.00).

  • Step 4: {Work-order-1}'s invoice has one row under {Sales-rep-A}, its Labor row: Labor Invoiced $600.00, Shop Supplies $30.00, Adjustments ($30.00), its share of the discount (600 ÷ 1,000 × 50), subtotal $600.00.
  • Step 5: its Parts row under {Sales-rep-B}: Parts Invoiced $400.00, Adjustments ($20.00), its share of the discount (400 ÷ 1,000 × 50), subtotal $380.00. The two subtotals add up to the invoice's total before tax: $600.00 + $380.00 = $980.00.

The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00. Each row shows its share in its Adjustments column.”
